briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Operators Find Political Cover as Federal Psychedelics and Cannabis Reform Accelerate
briefs.top: Michigan's cannabis trade group just picked a horse in the governor's race, betting a repeal of the 24% wholesale tax is finally within reach, while independent operators keep opening new doors despite the squeeze. Nationally, DEA rescheduling is grinding toward a 2026 rule and the FDA is fast-tracking psilocybin and MDMA therapies, giving both plant medicine sectors real momentum heading into Q4.

local.text: Industry endorses James, bets on tax repeal — MiCIA backed GOP nominee John James for governor, with director Robin Schneider calling him "the clear choice for the cannabis industry" over his pledge to kill the 24% wholesale tax.

Metro Times crowns Detroit's best weed of 2026 — staff picks spotlight home-grown standouts, praising Detroit's Hytek for its live rosin lineup and Hazel Park's woman-owned Hive for its farm-to-shelf flower.

Nature's Remedy expands while rivals shrink — the Ferndale dispensary known for connoisseur flower is opening new Pontiac and Redford stores, adding budtender, manager and security jobs even as dozens of metro Detroit shops close.

Second wholesale-tax challenge nears trial — MiCIA's original case is headed to trial this month while a newer suit argues the 24% levy creates unconstitutional "tax pyramiding" on top of the state's 6% sales tax cap.
Market holds near $260M a month, still No. 2 nationally — Michigan cannabis sales hit $260.6 million in July, keeping the state's market "robust" with over 30 million units sold despite tax pressure.

national.text: DEA rescheduling clears another procedural hurdle — the Schedule III review advanced on Aug. 18, with an NPRM expected before year-end 2026 and a final rule possible in 2027.

FDA fast-tracks three psychedelic therapies — Compass Pathways, Usona Institute and Transcend Therapeutics each landed Commissioner's National Priority Vouchers that compress FDA review from roughly ten months to about two.

Compass Pathways confirms psilocybin's durable effect — 26-week COMP006 data showed patients maintained response, with commercial launch readiness on track for end of 2026 and a launch expected in the first half of 2027.
FDA holds landmark hearing on psychedelic medicine — regulators convened a Sept. 14 public hearing on the future therapeutic use of psilocybin, MDMA and related compounds.
FDA finalizes psychedelic trial rulebook — new guidance covering psilocybin, LSD, MDMA and related serotonin agonists gives sponsors a clearer path through clinical development toward approval.
